title: BNP and NT-proBNP
subtitle: Heart-failure likelihood, confounders and referral thresholds
summary: Heart-failure likelihood, confounders and referral thresholds
introduction: Natriuretic peptides support assessment of heart failure but do not independently diagnose congestion. Interpret with symptoms, ECG, examination, renal function, rhythm, age, obesity and echocardiography.

rows.name: <400 ng/L
rows.referenceRange: Heart failure less likely in an untreated person
notes: Review alternative diagnoses, but levels can be lower with obesity or medications such as diuretics, ACE inhibitors/ARBs/ARNI, beta blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists.

rows.name: 400–2,000 ng/L
rows.referenceRange: NICE: specialist assessment and echocardiography within 6 weeks
notes: Does not prove heart failure. Renal impairment, AF, age, PE, sepsis and pulmonary hypertension can elevate the result.

rows.name: >2,000 ng/L
rows.referenceRange: NICE: urgent specialist assessment and echocardiography within 2 weeks
notes: Higher values are associated with worse prognosis, but acute disposition still depends on current symptoms and physiology.

urgentFindings: Breathlessness at rest, SpO₂ below expected range, inability to lie flat, pink frothy sputum, widespread crackles, hypotension or new confusion.
Rapidly increasing peripheral oedema with reduced urine output, chest pain or syncope.
Do not use a chronically raised BNP/NT-proBNP alone as evidence of acute fluid overload; compare with symptoms, examination, weight and previous results.
overrides: Use the reporting laboratory’s reference ranges and compare with previous results, symptoms, observations, medication and fluid status.

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Minor editorial change clinically reviewed and validated. No change to clinical meaning, thresholds, calculations, management, disposition or safety-netting.
